title: Predict the limiting pitch condition
brief: Record predictions before running five pitch-authority challenges. A lower-speed condition is not automatically a failure: calculate its margin.
supplied: How do lower speed, increased pitch inertia, a stronger opposing moment and effector degradation affect the trainer margin?
M_available=0.5*rho*V²*S*c*dCm; M_required=Iy*target-other; margin=M_available-M_required; initial acceleration=(M_available+other)/Iy at full command.
900 kg trainer; rho=1.20 kg/m³; V=20 m/s; S=27.25 m²; c=4 m; usable dCm=0.153; Iy=5000 kg m²; other=-750 N m; target=0.12 rad/s². Nose-up moment is positive about the declared CG.
Available moment, required moment and margin (N m); pass/fail for each explicitly changed condition.
Change one parameter at a time. Increasing Iy changes response demand, not aerodynamic capacity. A degraded coefficient is a synthetic sensitivity case, not a failure probability.
Initial single-axis pitch screen at the declared condition. Constant coefficients and inertia. No proof of successful takeoff, ground clearance, stall recovery, or safe landing.

Worked baseline: available 4002.48 N m; required 1350 N m; margin 2652.48 N m. For a changed case, recompute only the affected side of the budget and subtract. Record the changed-case prediction before inspecting its result.
Check 0.7² speed scaling; distinguish the unchanged capacity in the inertia challenge from the increased required moment.
Show a named challenge table and a speed sweep; keep predictions separate from observed results.
Evaluate the full moment budget once for each named single-parameter change. Compare signed margin with zero.

Decision method: retain only a condition whose available moment meets demand, under the stated assumptions. Explain which input change could require narrowing or revising the claim. Changed-case conclusions are made after inspection.

experience.scenario: The trainer has a positive baseline moment margin. You will predict the effect of five single-parameter changes before inspecting each result.
experience.task: Record a prediction for every named challenge, then run and inspect them. The baseline worked example remains visible; changed-case outcomes appear in the investigation.
experience.method: Speed and usable coefficient affect capacity. Inertia and opposing moment affect demand. A reduced margin does not necessarily mean failure: compare the resulting signed margin with zero. Original predictions are preserved in attempt history.
experience.investigate: For each named challenge, compare your original prediction with the observation. Explain which side of the moment budget changed.
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.
